mammals.name: Mammals
mammals.description: Warm-blooded animals that nurse their young — from tigers and elephants to whales and bats.

birds.name: Birds
birds.description: Feathered, egg-laying vertebrates that fill the skies, forests and wetlands with colour and song.

reptiles.name: Reptiles
reptiles.description: Scaly, cold-blooded survivors — crocodilians, snakes, lizards and turtles.

amphibians.name: Amphibians
amphibians.description: Frogs, toads and salamanders that live between water and land, and are sensitive indicators of a healthy environment.

fish.name: Fish
fish.description: Gill-breathing vertebrates of rivers and seas, from the hilsa to the giant whale shark.

insects.name: Insects
insects.description: The most diverse animals on Earth — pollinators, recyclers and food for countless other species.

plants.name: Plants
plants.description: Herbs, shrubs and medicinal plants that produce oxygen, food and traditional remedies.

trees.name: Trees
trees.description: Long-lived giants that store carbon, shelter wildlife and shape entire landscapes.

flowers.name: Flowers
flowers.description: Flowering plants celebrated for their beauty, pollinators and cultural meaning.

fungi.name: Fungi
fungi.description: Mushrooms, moulds and their hidden networks — nature's recyclers and partners of plants.

marine.name: Marine Life
marine.description: Life of oceans and coasts: whales, corals, dolphins, octopuses and more.

freshwater.name: Freshwater Life
freshwater.description: Species of rivers, lakes, ponds and floodplains — the lifeblood of Bangladesh.

tropical-forest.name: Tropical Forests
tropical-forest.description: Warm, wet forests near the equator that hold more than half of all land species.

temperate-forest.name: Temperate Forests
temperate-forest.description: Forests with distinct seasons, home to deciduous and coniferous trees.

mangrove.name: Mangrove Forests
mangrove.description: Salt-tolerant coastal forests like the Sundarbans that protect shores from storms.

grassland.name: Grasslands & Savannas
grassland.description: Open landscapes of grasses that support great herds and their predators.

wetland.name: Wetlands
wetland.description: Haors, beels, marshes and swamps — nurseries for fish and refuges for migratory birds.

rivers-lakes.name: Rivers & Lakes
rivers-lakes.description: Flowing and still freshwater systems that sustain fisheries, farms and wildlife.

ocean.name: Open Ocean
ocean.description: The vast blue — Earth's largest habitat, from sunlit surface to the deep sea.

coral-reef.name: Coral Reefs
coral-reef.description: Living underwater cities built by corals, sheltering a quarter of marine species.

desert.name: Deserts & Drylands
desert.description: Arid lands where life survives through remarkable adaptations.

mountain.name: Mountains
mountain.description: High-altitude ecosystems from cloud forests to alpine meadows and snowfields.

polar.name: Polar Regions
polar.description: Frozen seas and ice sheets of the Arctic and Antarctic.

urban-farmland.name: Farms, Villages & Cities
urban-farmland.description: Human-shaped landscapes where wildlife and people share space.

page.subtitle: Twelve windows into the tree of life. Choose a group to see its species.

habitatsPage.subtitle: Every species depends on a home. Discover the ecosystems that sustain life — from the Sundarbans to the coral reefs.
